source_snapshot.procedure: While the system is under OS status, POST Redfish ComputerSystem.Reset with `ResetType: ForceOff`; source embeds credentials in the URL, disables TLS verification and says to clear logs before test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Redfish response is readable, correct and error-free.
source_snapshot.script: Private power-off; 30 attended and 30 machine minutes.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; proposes ForceOff and IPMI post-state, warns about active jobs, but lacks secure transport, workload/filesystem gate, approval, ambiguity and recovery controls.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION at CRITICAL risk; verify isolated on/OS target and workload safety, immediate abrupt-power approval, secure action, independent monitoring, no retry or automatic power-on, preserve filesystem/storage/SEL evidence.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Recognizes disruption and the need for a dedicated idle SUT but does not establish that abrupt removal is acceptable rather than merely convenient.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly separates the automatable ForceOff request/readback from human ownership of data-loss risk and recovery.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ForceOff is not equivalent to a graceful shutdown. An apparently idle OS may still have dirty caches, mounted filesystems or controller writes, so acceptance requires an explicit abrupt-power test objective and owner risk decision, not only process-level inactivity.

original_test_intent: Verify that one authorized isolated SUT in a known OS-running and workload-safe state powers off after one supported Redfish ForceOff action, with abrupt-interruption risk explicitly accepted and recovery separately governed.
original_method: Prove exact target and on/OS state, record workload/storage/filesystem baseline, confirm ForceOff rather than graceful shutdown is intended, validate independent recovery, obtain immediate approval, issue one secure ForceOff POST, independently verify off state, preserve all evidence, and hand any future power-on to a separate authorization.
manual_activity: The workload/system owner confirms that abrupt power removal is the intended test, verifies no active jobs or unacceptable storage risk, explicitly approves ForceOff, observes the independent path and owns later recovery/power-on.
required_inputs: Verified Redfish/IPMI on and OS state
Workload, filesystem and storage safety evidence
safety_requirements: Never use ForceOff as generic cleanup
Never target an unidentified or shared system
Confirm no active or protected workload
Assess filesystem and storage write risk
Use trusted TLS and secret-safe sessions
agent_execution_scope: Verify target, on/OS state and workload safety
Validate ForceOff support and independent recovery
Archive evidence and hand off recovery without verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: ForceOff matches the source, but `-k`, command-line secrets and the absence of storage/filesystem, approval, independent recovery and single-issue controls make the example unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After protected reads prove the exact target is on, OS-running and approved for abrupt interruption, POST one vendor-supported `ResetType: ForceOff` through a trusted authenticated session; verify off independently and perform no automatic recovery.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The on-to-off ForceOff intent and 30/30-minute window remain; log clearing, graceful-shutdown substitution and automatic power-on are excluded unless separately authorized.

modernized_recommendation.status: AUTHORIZED ABRUPT POWER REMOVAL WITH RECOVERY HANDOFF
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a timeline from workload/storage safety evidence and approval through POST response, loss of host service, Redfish/IPMI off state and formal recovery ownership.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds an explicit abrupt-power risk gate and separates result verification from any recovery action.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: An HTTP response cannot prove physical off state, workload safety, absence of data impact or that a second action was not issued after ambiguous completion.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: ForceOff can cause unrecoverable application data loss or filesystem repair. Successful transition does not prove data integrity; those observations remain evidence for the engineer verdict.

project_override_considerations: The Project must explicitly require ForceOff rather than graceful shutdown and define acceptable storage/workload preconditions. If abrupt loss is prohibited, this case is BLOCKED; it must not be silently converted to a graceful shutdown case.
expected_evidence: Target/resource identity, on/OS state and isolated-SUT proof
Workload/filesystem/storage safety checks and explicit abrupt-power approval
Trusted TLS/auth/client metadata with secrets redacted
Complete ForceOff POST response/task and one-command audit
Preserved SEL/OS/storage evidence, recovery handoff and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and procedure consistently require ForceOff while under OS status. The response-only criterion is incomplete but not a competing outcome; abruptness is explicit in the payload.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Isolation, workload safety, secure action support and approval are obtainable project inputs. Execution becomes BLOCKED if abrupt-power authorization, safe preconditions or independent recovery cannot be established.

review_improvement: Makes the destructive nature of ForceOff explicit and prevents both graceful-shutdown substitution and unsafe automatic recovery.
independent_technical_reasoning: Host process inactivity does not prove storage quiescence, and ForceOff bypasses OS flush and shutdown sequencing. Thus target state, write-risk evidence and owner acceptance are independent prerequisites. After submission, an off-state read is the only safe way to resolve completion; a repeated POST or chained On would expand risk and invalidate the single-transition evidence.
